facts.title: chemical release during a planned shutdown on K-7301

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was lost time injury, with 1 person injured and 4 days lost.

defences.finding: Control FIRE_WATCH_PROVISION: the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control HAZARDOUS_AREA_EQUIPMENT_INTEGRITY: the integrity of explosion-protected equipment in zoned areas was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch on K-7301, PT-7301 and ZV-7212 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on K-7301, PT-7301 and ZV-7212 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in authorising hot work, specifically providing and briefing a fire watch. K-7301 (vapour recovery compressor) is in service for loading vapour recovery. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was in place but did not perform. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 31 October 2014 an incident occurred on K-7301, PT-7301 and ZV-7212 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
